chapter: Blanton, Los Angeles and Art Tatum
title: Tiny Grimes struggles; Tatum expects players to know every key
summary: Grimes sometimes laid out when Tatum changed keys; Crouch suggests Tatum wanted anyone who played with him to handle every key.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: How was -- how did Tiny Grimes respond to the band? How did the guys --
Well, Tiny -- it was quite a chore for Tiny. He possibly couldn't hear as well as I could. He was -- Every once in a while he would -- he wouldn't be playing. He
wouldn't be keeping up with it, you know. He laid out quite a few times.
Oh, I see, when it would change up and he wouldn't know where it was, and he wouldn't know what notes to play.
That's right, just lay out until he got himself together. And finally when he was used to, became used to the tricks being played, it became a little easier for him, I guess. Yes.
Well, that's almost -- that seems almost as though Tatum is trying to make it clear that, if you played with him, that you should know -- how to play in every key.
Yeah, because that kind of -- that's another way, it seems like, that he wanted to tell you guys how --
That's the way it seems, yes.
If you can't keep up with him, well, something else has to be done, you know.
